Cross-validation of an ABC model across sites

Source: R/abc_cv.R
abc_cv.Rd

For each fold, fits abc_fit() on the statistics of the sites kept, draws from the approximate posterior given the observed statistics of those sites, and predicts the statistics of the sites left out from the same rows of the reference table, as in abc_ppc(). A model that fits the sites it saw but not the others gives observed test statistics outside the predictive intervals. Use spatial blocks from spatial_folds() so that the test sites are not neighbours of the training sites.

Usage

abc_cv(
  table,
  observed,
  parameters = NULL,
  statistics = NULL,
  level = 0.9,
  n = 500,
  ntree = 500,
  ncores = 1,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

table

An mc_abc_table from abc_table() with summarise = fold_summarise(...).

observed

Named numeric vector with the same statistics for the observed data, from the same fold_summarise() function, or a data frame with one data set per row. The forests are fitted once per fold for all rows.

parameters

Names of the parameters. By default those of table.

statistics

Names of the statistics without the prefix, such as "alpha". By default all.

level

Probability of the predictive interval.

n

Number of draws from the posterior of each fold.

ntree

Number of trees per forest.

ncores

Number of threads for the forests.

seed

Integer that sets the seed.

Value

A data frame with one row per observed data set, fold and statistic: observed, the median and the interval of the predicted statistic, inside (whether the observed value is in the interval), p (two-sided posterior predictive p-value) and z, the observed value minus the predicted median over the predictive standard deviation. summary() averages over folds and data sets (n rows per statistic): the coverage, the mean of z, the root mean square of z and the fraction of p-values below 0.05.

See also

Other inference: abc_choose(), abc_diagnose(), abc_fit(), abc_ppc(), abc_recovery(), abc_table(), fold_summarise(), observe_detection(), spatial_folds()

Examples

set.seed(1)
table <- data.frame(a = runif(400))
for (f in 1:2) {
  table[[paste0("f", f, "_train_s")]] <- table$a + rnorm(400, 0, 0.05)
  table[[paste0("f", f, "_test_s")]] <- table$a + rnorm(400, 0, 0.1)
}
observed <- c(f1_train_s = 0.5, f1_test_s = 0.55, f2_train_s = 0.5, f2_test_s = 0.9)
cv <- abc_cv(table, observed, parameters = "a", ntree = 100)
cv
#>   observation fold statistic observed    median       low      high inside   p
#> 1           1    1         s     0.55 0.5007813 0.2110433 0.6163250   TRUE 0.7
#> 2           1    2         s     0.90 0.5203422 0.4107620 0.5585261  FALSE 0.0
#>           z
#> 1 0.4384356
#> 2 6.7852324
summary(cv)
#>   statistic n coverage   z_mean   z_rms rejected
#> 1         s 2      0.5 3.611834 4.80789      0.5
